messages:
sam: :rotating_light: Canary alert: p95 token latency jumped in eu-west dedicated pools after rolling runtime v4.4.0 (was stable on v4.3.1). Canary started ~03:15 UTC. root merge 6fa2b9c. SLA risk if this propagates to reserved tenants.
anya: Saw the CI perf job reported a small regression but it didn't fail gating. Looks like the perf window was narrow so the job passed thresholds.
ci-bot: perf/job/runtime-eu-west: p95 increased from 84.5ms -> 218.7ms (3rd percentile of runs flagged). See: https://ci.redwood/ci/abc123/perf
mike: I ran a local bisect, narrows to merge 6fa2b9c -> changeset that toggled kvcache eviction behavior + batching heuristic tweak. Minimal diff: flip eviction_policy to "aggressive" and change batch_size estimator.
jesse: Adding the perf dump from a canary pod (snip):
```
kvcache.size_bytes=1288490188
kvcache.evictions_per_sec=128
kvcache.eviction_policy=aggressive
batch_estimator.alpha=0.9
runtime.kernel.selected=auto-merge-3
p95_token_latency_ms=212
queue_depth_avg=63
```
mike: The eviction change was intended to reduce memory pressure during high-concurrency workloads, but aggressive evictions cause more KV misses + recompute + more kernel context switches. Combined with the new batching estimator, it looks like we overshot and now more long-seq requests hit slow path.
elaine: Which customers are on the affected dedicated pools? Any paying clusters in eu-west?
sam: Two large reserved customers (acme-corp, shopline) pinned to those pools. Their error budgets are already tight; legal is breathing down me.
infra-sre: Canary metrics show cross-region tail: eu-west -> p95 + queueing increased, us-west unaffected. Hypothesis: different seq-length mix + slightly smaller GPU memory on eu-west instance types makes aggressive eviction harmful.
anya: Can we short-circuit by disabling the new eviction flag remotely without a full rollback? I can push a runtime env var change and rolling restart the canary nodes.
mike: Yes, set KV_CACHE_EVICTION=legacy and restart runtime pods. That should drop evictions and restore cache hit rate.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by sam: env change KV_CACHE_EVICTION=legacy to runtime-canary-eu-west at 03:42 UTC. Rolling restart 3/6 pods.
jesse: After 2 pods restarted: p95 dropping to ~95ms, evictions/sec -> 12. Good signal.
ci-bot: Note: CI perf job earlier showed elevated p95 on longseq tests; test matrix did not include eu-west instance types which hid the effect.
elaine: We should block promotion to remaining regions until we confirm.
sam: Agreed. Hold global rollout. Stop next waves.
mike: Plan: 1) Pause rollout 2) Hotfix env var to disable aggressive eviction on canaries (done) 3) Re-run targeted perf harness with eu-west instance profiles + longseq workload 4) Bisect the batching estimator tweak separately 5) If safe, reintroduce a tuned eviction threshold (not "aggressive") + kernel pin.
infra-sre: Kernel selection interplay: runtime.kernel.selected=auto-merge-3 seems to pick a slow kernel variant under high-KV-miss conditions. We might want to pin to kernel v3.1 which had better cache/memory locality.
anya: I ran a quick A/B by pinning kernel v3.1 on one canary pod + legacy eviction: that pod p95=78ms, others ~92ms. Kernel pin helps but eviction flip was the main culprit.
jesse: Will open a rollback PR for the merge that toggled eviction + remove the batching estimator change from the head. Also attaching perf flame snippet: high time spent in kv_lookup() and scheduler::reschedule_on_miss().
mike: Can we add a temporary routing rule to avoid routing large longseq traffic to eu-west dedicated pools? Might protect tenants until fix.
elaine: Ops preference is env-var hotfix + pause rollout + targeted rerun. Routing rules are heavier and might impact throughput guarantees.
sam: I'll notify support + affected customers with status and ETA. Also file an incident.
deploy-bot: rollout paused for v4.4.0 at 03:50 UTC.
infra-sre: Follow-up actions: re-run perf harness with: --seq-dist long-tail --instance-profile eu-west-g4x --kvcache-size=1.2GB, add metric kvcache.evictions_per_sec, and measure kernel context switch rate.
anya: I'll own the perf reruns and the bisect for batching estimator. Mike, can you handle the rollback PR + kernel pin test? Jesse, coordinate with infra for canary restarts.
mike: On it. Will create PR and request approvals.
jesse: I will collect heap dumps and a few trace samples from the affected pods for post-mortem.
elaine: Thanks team. Please update thread with any customer impact / pager escalation. :thumbsup:
sam: Noted — will update support after we confirm stabilized metrics.
ci-bot: Reminder: add an integration test case for eu-west instance profile to perf matrix to catch this earlier.
